reproduction_manifest.notes: Reproduction successful on BFCL v4 Non-Live (600 samples: 200 Multiple + 400 Simple Python). Function Accuracy 100.0% (paper 99.8%), Overall Accuracy 87.2% (paper 79.8%). Both metrics exceed lower bounds. The higher Overall Accuracy is attributed to BFCL v4 data (closest available; paper used v3) and possibly different evaluation checker leniency. Model: RT-Qwen2.5-0.5B FP16 (LoRA-merged Qwen2.5-0.5B with special tokens for multi-head parallel decoding). AWQ model also tested: 99.2% Function Accuracy, 77.2% Overall Accuracy (slightly below lower bound due to quantization). V1 prompt format required for 0.5B model (explicit multi-head instructions).
reproduction_manifest.eval_output_format: stdout: Overall Accuracy (%), Function Accuracy (%); also saved to --output JSON file with per-sample results
reproduction_manifest.known_levers: LoRA rank (higher = more capacity), training data composition (xLAM + synthetic augmentation), number of parallel argument heads (6 covers 95.2% of cases), prompt format (v1 vs v2), temperature (default 0.0), system prompt engineering, parameter ordering in tool definitions
reproduction_manifest.setup_notes: Container: autosota_repro_paper_2141 from docker.1ms.run/pytorch/pytorch:2.1.0-cuda12.1-cudnn8-runtime. Python 3.10, pip-installed vLLM 0.12.0 (downgraded from 0.24.0 due to CUDA/flashinfer compatibility), flashinfer-cubin downgraded to 0.5.3 to match flashinfer-python. CUDA_HOME set to /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/nvidia/cu13 (pip-installed CUDA toolkit). gcc/g++ installed (build-essential). Model downloaded from Cialtion/SimpleTool on HuggingFace to /models/RT-Qwen2.5-0.5B. BFCL v4 evaluation data cloned from https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla to /repo/gorilla. AWQ model (RT-Qwen2.5-0.5B-AWQ) also downloaded but config required patching (removed scale_dtype/zp_dtype from quantization_config) for vLLM 0.12.0 compatibility. All downloads used https://hf-mirror.com for HuggingFace and https://pypi.tuna.tsinghua.edu.cn for pip.

optimization_objective.summary: Improve Overall Accuracy on BFCL function-calling benchmark while maintaining high Function Accuracy. The paper focuses on both accuracy and speed; for SOTA optimization, accuracy is the primary target given that speed depends on quantization and inference infrastructure.

metrics.name: Overall Accuracy
metrics.rationale: Primary metric: complete correctness of function name AND all arguments. Paper reports 79.8% on BFCL-v3; our baseline is 87.2% on BFCL-v4 with FP16 model.

metrics.name: Function Accuracy
metrics.rationale: Function name selection accuracy. Paper reports 99.8%. Must not regress below 98.3% (lower bound) as getting the wrong function invalidates all arguments.

optimization_objective.success_policy: Prioritize Overall Accuracy improvement. Function Accuracy must remain above 98.3%. If both improve, consider the iteration successful. If Overall Accuracy improves but Function Accuracy drops below 98.3%, the iteration is rejected.
